question.prompt:
Squares \(ABCD,\) \(EFGH,\) and \(GHIJ\) are equal in area. Points \(C\) and \(D\) are the midpoints of sides \(IH\) and \(HE,\) respectively. What is the ratio of the area of the shaded pentagon \(AJICB\) to the sum of the areas of the three squares?

[Figure 1](figures/2013_AMC_8_Q24_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The pentagon's sloping side suggests enclosing it in a right triangle, whose area is easy to calculate. Equal-area squares have equal side lengths. Use half of their common side as one length unit, so every square has side length \(2\). Measuring all areas in the same square units preserves the requested ratio.

The midpoint conditions give \(DH=HC=CI=1\). Extend \(AB\) past \(B\) to meet the extension of \(JI\) past \(I\) at \(K\). Then \(BKIC\) is a rectangle, with \(BK=CI=1\) and \(KI=BC=2\). Consequently,
\[
AK=AB+BK=3,\qquad KJ=KI+IJ=4.
\]
Triangle \(AKJ\) consists exactly of the shaded pentagon and rectangle \(BKIC\), with disjoint interiors. Thus the shaded area is
\[
\frac12\cdot3\cdot4-1\cdot2=4.
\]
Each square also has area \(2^2=4\), so the requested ratio is
\[
\frac{4}{3\cdot4}=\boxed{\frac13},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Complete a larger triangle

solutions.explanation:
The two squares above and below the horizontal line have equal heights. This suggests moving the lower shaded triangle into the triangular gap in square \(ABCD\).

Let the common side length of the squares be \(s>0\). Since \(D\) is the midpoint of \(HE\),
\[
DI=DH+HI=\frac{s}{2}+s=\frac{3s}{2}.
\]
Let \(P\) be the midpoint of \(DI\). Then \(DP=3s/4<DC=s\), so \(P\) lies between \(D\) and \(C\).

A half-turn about \(P\) sends \(D\) to \(I\). In the displayed arrangement, \(DA\) and \(IJ\) are perpendicular to \(DI\), have equal length \(s\), and lie on opposite sides of \(DI\). Therefore the same half-turn sends \(A\) to \(J\). In particular, \(A,P,J\) are collinear, and the half-turn sends triangle \(ADP\) exactly onto triangle \(JIP\). These triangles have equal areas because rotation preserves size.

The shaded pentagon is square \(ABCD\) with triangle \(ADP\) removed and triangle \(JIP\) added. The equal triangular areas cancel, leaving the area of one square. The three square areas total three times that amount, so the ratio is \(\boxed{\frac13}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Exchange two equal triangles
